Test for density correlation between two cell types.

Source: R/corDensity.R
corDensity.Rd

Test for density correlation between two cell types.

Usage

corDensity(
  spe,
  coi = NULL,
  roi = NULL,
  probs = 0.85,
  min.density = NULL,
  trace = FALSE,
  method = c("permutation", "modified.ttest"),
  id = "cell_type",
  nperm = 999,
  permute.within = NULL,
  cpu_threads = 1
)

Arguments

spe

A SpatialExperiment object.

coi

Character vector for cell types of interest for density correlation analysis. Default is NULL, which is to consider all cell types previously calculated in the gridDensity() step.

roi

Character. The name of the group or cell type on which the roi is computed. Default is NULL for no subsetting cell types by ROI

probs

A numeric scalar. The threshold of proportion that used to filter grids by density when ROIs have not been identified previously. Ignored if 'roi' is present in the 'metadata' component of spe. Default to 0.85.

min.density

A numeric value. The cut-off on the same density score as 'probs': grids with a score of at least 'min.density' are kept. Ignored if 'roi' is given. Default is NULL and overwrites probs.

trace

Logical. If TRUE, print the process of testing. Default to FALSE.

method

Character. The testing method, either "permutation" (default) or "modified.ttest". See Details.

id

Character. The column of colData(spe) holding the cell type labels that were used in gridDensity(). Only used by method "permutation". Default to "cell_type".

nperm

Integer. The number of random relabellings used by method "permutation". Default to 999.

permute.within

Character or NULL. The column of colData(spe) that splits cells into groups (e.g. tissue compartments) for method "permutation". Cell type labels are then shuffled only among cells of the same group. Default to NULL, which shuffles labels across all cells. See Details.

cpu_threads

Integer. The number of threads used by method "permutation". The results do not depend on it. Default to 1.

Value

A list of two DataFrames, 'ROI' (results per ROI) and 'overall' (results combined across ROIs). When 'roi' is NULL the selected grids form a single ROI, labelled "1", and the overall results equal the ROI level results. For method "permutation" the columns are celltype1, celltype2, ROI, ngrid, cor.coef (observed Spearman correlation), cor.expected (mean under random labelling), shift, p.Pos and p.Neg; the overall DataFrame has n.roi, n.above, n.below, n.sig.Pos and n.sig.Neg (see Details) in place of ROI and ngrid. For method "modified.ttest" the columns are celltype1, celltype2, ROI, ngrid, cor.coef, t, df, p.Pos and p.Neg.

Details

Method "permutation" tests each pair of cell types against random labelling. Every cell keeps its location and the cell type labels are shuffled across all cells of the sample, after which the cell type densities are recomputed with the same kernel and bandwidth as in gridDensity(). The statistic is the Spearman correlation between the two densities across grids: within each ROI for the ROI level results, and pooled over all ROIs after centering the ranks at the ROI level for the overall results. The column 'cor.expected' gives the mean of the statistic under random labelling, which is the correlation expected from the shared dependence of both densities on local cellularity alone. 'p.Pos' and 'p.Neg' are one sided Monte Carlo p-values, (1 + b) / (1 + nperm), for the observed correlation being larger or smaller than expected under random labelling. The 'shift' (cor.coef - cor.expected) measures the strength of co-localization (positive) or segregation (negative) beyond random labelling. The overall results also give a per pair summary of the ROI level results: 'n.roi' ROIs with a defined correlation, 'n.above' and 'n.below' ROIs with the observed correlation above or below its expected value, and 'n.sig.Pos' and 'n.sig.Neg' ROIs with p.Pos or p.Neg below 0.05. With many grids, small shifts reach significance, so rank pairs by the shift and check the ROI summary for consistency. Use set.seed() for reproducible p-values; the results do not depend on 'cpu_threads'.

With 'permute.within', the null hypothesis is random labelling within groups: each group keeps its cell locations and cell type counts, and only the labels inside a group are shuffled. Structure already encoded by the groups, such as the split between tumour and stroma compartments, then becomes part of the expected value, and the test asks whether cell types are organized beyond it. For two cell types in the same group a positive shift means they share neighbourhoods more than two random cells of that group would; for cell types in different groups it means they sit closer to each other than random cells of their groups would. Groups should be coarse: a cell type that is the only type in every group it occupies is never moved, so pairs involving it are only tested through the other cell type.

Method "modified.ttest" is the original approach: a Pearson correlation within each ROI tested by the modified t-test of Dutilleul (1993) from SpatialPack, with the ROI level p-values combined by Fisher's method. Its effective degrees of freedom are estimated from the spatial correlogram within each ROI.

Examples


data("xenium_bc_spe")

coi <- c("Breast cancer", "Fibroblasts", "B cells", "T cells")

spe <- gridDensity(spe, coi = coi)

spe <- findROI(spe, coi = coi, method = "walktrap")

set.seed(1)
result <- corDensity(spe, roi = coi, nperm = 199)
